summary: This section of the act details the establishment and governance of public schools in Newport. It explicitly states that the public schools are to be maintained for 'all white children residing in said city, between the ages of six and twenty years'. This segregation of educational facilities based on race is a hallmark of Jim Crow laws.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 376, p. 459
title: AN ACT for the benefit of Robert Barlow, colored pauper idiot, of Hart county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 376, p. 459
summary: This act directs the Auditor of Public Accounts to issue a warrant for forty dollars and seventy-nine cents to Harvey Barlow, committee of Robert Barlow, a colored pauper idiot of Hart County, for the idiot's support from January 6, 1873, to October 28, 1873. The act is effective upon passage.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 387, pp. 472–475
title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled" An act to incorporate Princeton College," approved February 20th, 1860, and to confer certain powers on the board of trustees of the town of Princeton.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 387, pp. 472–475
summary: This act allows the board of trustees of Stanford, Kentucky, to levy taxes for the support of a college or schools. Crucially, it specifies that property taxes for municipal purposes and poll taxes for white male citizens over twenty-one years of age are subject to voter approval by qualified white voters. The tax collection is also explicitly limited to property belonging to white persons.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 396, pp. 480–481
title: AN ACT to establish and provide for a colored free school in the city of Owensboro, Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 396, pp. 480–481
summary: This act authorizes the city of Owensboro to levy a special tax on males of African descent over 21 and on property owned by persons of African descent to fund a separate free school for colored children. The tax rates are specified, and the collection and disbursement of funds are outlined, including the appointment and duties of a board of trustees for the colored school.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 494, pp. 100–101
title: AN ACT to amend chapter eighteen of General Statutes, entitled" Common Schools."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 494, pp. 100–101
summary: This act amends several sections of Kentucky law, primarily related to the timing of elections, appointments, and financial distributions within educational contexts. Notably, it explicitly amends Article Seven, Section One to refer to 'the qualified white voters of the district' instead of 'county,' and Article Seven, Section Eight to specify 'a majority of the white qualified voters of such district.' These changes indicate a racial qualification for participation in district matters, likely related to school governance or funding.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 495, pp. 590–592
title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the city of Cynthiana.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 495, pp. 590–592
summary: This act amends the charter of the city of Cynthiana, establishing the election of two public school trustees and granting them control over the common school. Crucially, it specifies that the tax levied for the support of the school shall be levied only on the property of white people.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 521, pp. 102–105
title: AN ACT to establish a uniform system of common schools for the colored children of this Commonwealth.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 521, pp. 102–105
summary: This act establishes a separate and distinct system of common schools for the education of colored children in Kentucky. It outlines the funding sources for this 'colored school fund,' which include specific taxes on colored persons, capitation taxes on colored males, taxes on dogs owned by colored persons, state taxes collected from colored persons, and fines/penalties collected from colored persons.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 533, pp. 633–634
title: AN ACT to incorporate the Taylor County College.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 533, pp. 633–634
summary: This act allows common school trustees in a district where Eminence College is located to subscribe to its capital stock. If they do, the county judge is authorized to levy a tax on the property of *white* tax-payers of the district to pay for this subscription. The college, in turn, must agree to teach common schools for *white* children in that district and receive public money for it. The act also specifies that the sense of *white* qualified voters must be taken before any subscription is made.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 58, p. 168
title: AN ACT for the benefit of the Agricultural and Mechanical Association of the Colored People of Bourbon County.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 58, p. 168
summary: This act prohibits the sale of refreshments and spirituous or intoxicating drinks within a half mile of the grounds of the Agricultural and Mechanical Association of the Colored People of Bourbon County during its fair, unless authorized by local authorities. Violators are subject to penalties prescribed in a previous act.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 592, pp. 698–701
title: AN ACT to authorize and establish a system of public schools in the town of Ashland.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, ch. 592, pp. 698–701
summary: This act amends the establishment and regulation of public schools in Ashland. It grants the board of education the power to levy taxes for school purposes, including purchasing property, erecting buildings, and paying teachers. Notably, Section 16 explicitly states that only property belonging to white persons shall be taxed. Section 12 also mentions a poll-tax not to exceed one dollar on each white tithin in the district. Section 19 allows the admission of white children who are non-residents under certain conditions. Section 20 states the tax will not be levied until submitted to legally qualified white voters.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, p. 121
title: RESOLUTION directing the Governor to provide for such pauper lunatics as cannot be accommodated in the several lunatic asylums.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1874, p. 121
summary: This resolution directs the Governor to manage the overflow of pauper lunatics in Kentucky's asylums. It explicitly states that the asylum for colored lunatics is full, and the asylums for white lunatics are nearly full. The resolution mandates that colored and white lunatics shall not be kept in the same buildings, indicating a policy of racial segregation in the care of the mentally ill.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 212, pp. 382–388
title: AN ACT to provide and maintain public schools in Cloverport, Breckinridge county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 212, pp. 382–388
summary: This act consolidates two common school districts in Cloverport, Breckinridge county, into a single district. The control and management of this new district will be by a board of five trustees. Crucially, these trustees are to be elected annually by qualified white voters and any white widow entitled to a vote. This explicitly limits voting rights for school board elections to white individuals.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 338, pp. 544–545
title: AN ACT for the benefit of colored common schools in Trimble county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 338, pp. 544–545
summary: This act addresses a specific financial shortfall for colored common schools in Trimble County. It details how a colored schoolteacher, Maria F. Carter, was not paid for her services due to a failure in the reporting process by school officials. The act aims to rectify this by ensuring funds are allocated for her unpaid services.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 381, p. 577
title: AN ACT for the benefit of Thomas Shanks, sheriff of the county of Jefferson.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 381, p. 577
summary: This act allows Thomas Shanks, sheriff of Jefferson County, an extension to submit his delinquent list of 'negro tax' for the year 1874. If approved by the county court of claims and certified to the Auditor, the Auditor is authorized to allow Shanks credit for this amount on his 'negro tax' list for either 1875.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 390, pp. 586–628
title: AN ACT to reduce into one all the acts relating to the city of Owensboro. ARTICLE 1.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 390, pp. 586–628
summary: This statute outlines the taxing authority of the City of Owensboro for municipal purposes, including specific taxes for railroad bonds and public schools. Crucially, it explicitly states that taxes for school purposes can only be levied on white persons and corporations, while exempting the property of negroes from all taxes connected with public schools. It also specifies a separate capitation tax for white males for school expenses.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 76, pp. 269–270
title: AN ACT for the benefit of the public schools of the city of Louisville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 76, pp. 269–270
summary: This act authorizes the city of Louisville to levy an annual tax for five years to fund public schools for white children. The tax is to be levied on real estate, improvements, mixed property, and personal property exceeding the owner's debts. The funds are to be credited to the school fund and paid to the board of trustees of the Male High School, Female High School, and public schools.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 900, pp. 136–149
title: AN ACT to amend and reduce into one the several acts organizing and regulating the lunatic asylums of this State.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1876, ch. 900, pp. 136–149
summary: This act establishes separate admission districts for white and colored lunatics and idiots to the Eastern, Central, and Western Kentucky Lunatic Asylums. It specifies which counties' residents of each race are to be sent to which asylum, with provisions for overflow.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 514, pp. 199–202
title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled " An act to amend and reduce into one the several acts in relation to the town of Danville," approved March 10th, 1873.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 514, pp. 199–202
summary: This act authorizes the board of trustees to purchase land for a cemetery and issue bonds for its payment. It explicitly states that a tax will be levied on property owned by white persons to pay the interest on these bonds. Furthermore, it mandates that lots in the cemetery be sold to and used by white persons only.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 524, pp. 209–215
title: AN ACT to incorporate the Cemetery Company of Browinski Lodge, No. 64, I.O. O. F., in Carrollcounty.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 524, pp. 209–215
summary: This act incorporates Browinski Lodge, No. 64, I. O. O. F., and establishes rules for its cemetery. Section 16 explicitly prohibits the sale or ownership of cemetery lots to 'any person of color' and forbids lot holders from allowing persons of color to be buried in their lots, under penalty of forfeiture.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 744, pp. 547–550
title: AN ACT to incorporate the District of Cold Spring, in Campbell county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 744, pp. 547–550
summary: This statute outlines the governance of public schools in a specific district. It details the appointment and dismissal of teachers, curriculum, qualifications for teachers and pupils, and provisions for free tuition for white children between the ages of six and twenty. It also allows for the establishment of tax levies for school property and maintenance, specifically mentioning property belonging to white persons.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 745, pp. 551–556
title: AN ACT to establish and maintain a graded free school in the town of Harrodsburg, Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 745, pp. 551–556
summary: This act establishes a graded free school in Harrodsburg, Kentucky, and constitutes the town as a common school district. It specifies that the school district shall be under the exclusive control of six trustees who must be white men and resident voters. The election of trustees is to be conducted by qualified white voters. The act details the election process, terms of office, and the filling of vacancies for these trustees.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 798, pp. 610–611
title: AN ACT in aid of colored common schools in Hart county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 798, pp. 610–611
summary: This act addresses an error in reporting for colored common schools in Hart County for the school year ending June 30th, 1875. Specifically, two districts numbered 'No. 4' were reported to the commissioner, but one was mistakenly omitted by the Superintendent of Public Instruction, preventing an apportionment. The act aims to rectify this oversight and ensure proper funding for these schools.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 880, pp. 674–675
title: AN ACT to make additional provision for the education of the colored children in the city of Covington.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 880, pp. 674–675
summary: This act authorizes the board of school trustees of Covington to establish and maintain schools for colored children using funds derived from city taxation. The number and location of these schools are to be determined by the board to ensure sufficient educational facilities for the colored children.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 905, pp. 691–692
title: AN ACT in aid of R. H. Caldwell, common school commissioner of Boyle county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, ch. 905, pp. 691–692
summary: This act directs the Superintendent of Public Instruction to withhold funds from the apportionment of colored school money for the year ending June 30th, 1877, and pay $30 to R. H. Caldwell. This payment is to compensate Caldwell for an amount he was required to advance in the current year, due to his omission to report one hundred pupil children of colored school district No. 5, Boyle county, to the Superintendent of Public Instruction.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, p. 749
title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the city of Cynthiana.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, p. 749
summary: This act mandates that offenders fined in the mayor's court of Cynthiana for violating city ordinances or state laws, who fail to pay or replevy their fines and costs, shall be compelled to labor on public works in the city with a ball and chain until the fines and costs are discharged, at a rate of one dollar per day.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, pp. 759–760
title: AN ACT for the protection of sheep in the counties of Henderson, Breckinridge, Caldwell, Hancock, McLean, and Christian.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1876, pp. 759–760
summary: This act imposes a tax on dogs and bitches over six months of age in several Kentucky counties. Crucially, it mandates that funds from taxes on dogs owned by white persons go to the common school fund for white children, while funds from taxes on dogs owned by colored persons go to the common school fund for colored children. This establishes a racially segregated system for the allocation of tax revenue for education.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 1089, pp. 704–705
title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled " An act to establish and maintain a graded free school in Harrodsburg, Kentucky."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 1089, pp. 704–705
summary: This act amends a previous law establishing a graded free school in Harrodsburg, Kentucky. It allows for a vote by qualified white voters to determine if the school should be funded by taxation. The tax would be levied on property owned by white persons in the town, not exceeding thirty cents per one hundred dollars, to be used for common school education, excluding building erection. The act specifies that printed notices of the vote must be posted and published in a local paper.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 572, p. 54
title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled" An act to incorporate the Smithfield Cemetery Company."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 572, p. 54
summary: This act amends an earlier act to grant the Smithfield Cemetery Company the authority to condemn land for a passway. This passway is specifically designated to provide access from the Smithfield and New Castle Turnpike to the part of the cemetery used as a burial ground for persons of color. The passway is to be no more than twenty feet wide and is intended for the convenience of the colored people.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 587, p. 452
title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled " An act for the benefit of school district No. 39, in Bath county," approved February 9th, 1876.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 587, p. 452
summary: This act amends a previous act concerning school district No. 39 in Bath County. It specifies that only qualified white male voters and white widows with children between the ages of six and twenty years residing in the district have the privilege of voting for the trustees of the Sharpsburg Male and Female College. Widows can vote in person or by proxy. It also sets residency requirements for voters and limits each voter to one vote for each of the five trustees.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 662, pp. 222–233
title: AN ACT to organize and establish a system of public schools in the Elizabethtown common school district, in Hardin county, for white children in said district.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 662, pp. 222–233
summary: This act establishes a public school system within the Elizabethtown common school district in Hardin County, specifically for white children. It defines the territory covered by the district and states that the system is for white children.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 734, pp. 301–304
title: AN ACT to incorporate the West Louisville School District, in Daviess county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 734, pp. 301–304
summary: This act establishes the West Louisville School District and its board of trustees. Crucially, it explicitly exempts the property of colored citizens residing in the district from taxation for school purposes, while levying taxes on white male residents. This creates a racially segregated and unequal system of school funding.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 775, pp. 343–344
title: AN ACT to establish a public school for children of the African race in the city of Paducah.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 775, pp. 343–344
summary: This act mandates the establishment and maintenance of a public school specifically for children of the African race in Paducah, to be known as the Colored Public School of Paducah. It outlines the supervisory roles of the general public school trustees, including appointing teachers, setting rules, and adopting textbooks. It also establishes an advisory board of five qualified colored voters to assist in the school's governance.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 799, pp. 373–378
title: AN ACT to incorporate" The Board of Trustees for the Graded City School of Cynthiana, Kentucky."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 799, pp. 373–378
summary: This act incorporates "The Board of Trustees for the Graded City School of Cynthiana, Kentucky" as a body-corporate and politic. It vests absolute control of the graded city school in this board and empowers them to manage it effectively. Crucially, Section 2 explicitly states that only a white male, resident of Cynthiana, and over twenty-one years of age is eligible for the office of trustee.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 880, pp. 443–446
title: AN ACT to incorporate the Colored Orphans 'Aid Association of the city of Louisville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 880, pp. 443–446
summary: This act incorporates the Colored Orphans' Aid Association of Louisville, which aims to establish an asylum for colored orphan children. The association was formed by benevolent individuals who subscribed funds to aid in this endeavor, particularly for purchasing property for the institution.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 888, pp. 453–454
title: AN ACT to incorporate the Pine Grove Cemetery, in Muhlenburg county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 888, pp. 453–454
summary: This act incorporates the Pine Grove Cemetery in Muhlenburg County. It specifies that land purchased for the cemetery is to be laid off into burial lots exclusively for sale to white people. Certificates of sale are assignable and transferable, provided the sale is to a white person. The act also outlines provisions for the perpetual care of the cemetery funded by a bequest.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 919, pp. 496–497
title: AN ACT to authorize the trustees of common school district No. 50, in Mason county, to levy and collect a tax for the erection of school buildings.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 919, pp. 496–497
summary: This act authorizes the trustee of common school district No. 50 in Mason County to hold an election for qualified white voters to approve a tax on taxable property belonging to white persons. The tax revenue would be used to build a schoolhouse exclusively for white pupils. The tax rate was set at forty cents per one hundred dollars of taxable property, to be levied annually for up to five years, or until a total of two thousand dollars was collected.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 924, pp. 502–503
title: AN ACT to authorize the erection of a school building in colored school district No. 1, in Ohio county, and to levy a tax therefor.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 924, pp. 502–503
summary: This act authorizes the trustee of colored school district No. 1 in Ohio County to erect a schoolhouse, not exceeding $1000 in value, for the use of colored school children. The building is to be used solely as a schoolhouse.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 925, pp. 503–504
title: AN ACT to incorporate the Mt. Sterling Library Association."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1878, ch. 925, pp. 503–504
summary: This act, passed in 1878, grants the Mt. Sterling Library Association the power to levy taxes on real and personal property owned by colored citizens in a specific district, not exceeding one dollar per one hundred dollars worth. It also allows for a capitation tax on colored persons over twenty-one, not exceeding five dollars. Furthermore, it authorizes the trustee to call out male colored citizens between eighteen and fifty years of age for labor on a building, not exceeding two days per week, with penalties for failure to work similar to those for road hands. The act specifies that the taxes are to be collected like school taxes and that the act will only be in force if ratified by a majority of colored voters in the district.

It details the sheriff's role in collecting and allocating taxes for the colored school fund, the auditor's responsibility for maintaining a separate account, and the census and distribution methods for this fund, which are to mirror those for white children. It details the sheriff's role in collecting and allocating taxes for the colored school fund, the auditor's responsibility for maintaining a separate account, and the census and distribution methods for this fund, which are to mirror those for white children. statute_citation: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 14, p. 259

It details penalties for fraudulent census reporting and failure to comply with reporting requirements. citations: The General Statutes of Kentucky, 1879, § 15, p. 688

Assessors are subject to a fine for improperly enrolling names and must follow existing laws to prevent illegal voting. They are also required to take an oath to fairly ascertain qualified voters and report the numbers. Assessors are empowered to examine potential voters under oath.

summary: This act creates the office of Collector of Taxes for the city of Henderson and establishes eligibility requirements for this office. Specifically, Section 6 states that only a 'white male citizen' of Henderson, at least twenty-five years old, and a bona fide resident for at least two years prior to election, is eligible to hold the office of tax collector. The act also abolishes the office of judge of the Henderson city court and transfers its duties to the mayor.

The lessees can improve the property, with the right to remove additions if the lease is not renewed, provided no damage is done to the district's property.

The trustees have powers related to town planning, streets, alleys, sidewalks, and levying taxes.

The tax can be paid in one or two levies, as determined by a majority of the white voters. The act details the process for submitting the question, including notice requirements and election procedures, explicitly limiting voting to "qualified white voters."

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 22

citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 22
summary: This section of the Public School Law of Louisville, enacted in 1882, addresses various aspects of school administration, including filling vacancies, fines, and the admission of children. Crucially, section 101 explicitly states that 'colored children not to go to schools for white children' and mandates that taxes for colored schools be kept separate, indicating a clear policy of racial segregation in public education.

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 54

citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 54
summary: This act amends the charter of the City of Louisville to allow children of non-resident taxpayers to attend city schools free of tuition. Crucially, it explicitly prohibits children of the African race from attending schools with white children and mandates that school taxes paid by persons of the African race be kept as a separate fund for the education of African race children within the city.

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, pp. 55–58

It also mentions appropriations for schoolhouses for colored children and the establishment of a uniform system of schools for them.

The preamble explicitly states that relieving the school revenues of bond payments will enable the School Board to provide adequate educational facilities for colored children.

citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 80

It mandates the census of colored children and the distribution of the colored school fund in the same manner as for white children. Crucially, it explicitly prohibits colored children from attending schools for white children and vice versa.

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 81

citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 81
summary: This act authorizes the Board of Trustees of the public schools of Louisville to use surplus funds to erect or purchase two additional school houses for colored children, one in the eastern and one in the western part of the city.

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 82
title: AN ACT for the benefit of the Public Shoo ls of the City of Louisville. Approved February 1,1876. Acts of 1876, vol.1, p.234.
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 82
summary: This act levies a tax of 8 cents per $100 of property value to fund public schools in Louisville. Crucially, it specifies that these schoolhouses are 'for the use of white children'. The tax is subject to a voter referendum for its continuation.

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 39
title: Public School Law of Louisville - 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 39
summary: This statute outlines the powers and responsibilities of the Board of Trustees for the Public Schools of Louisville. It details their authority to elect and remove teachers, fix salaries, prescribe curriculum, set admission qualifications and numbers, and establish school districts. Crucially, it states that 'all freewhite children over six years of age within each district shall have equal rights of admission to the schools of that district.' It also prohibits sectarian teaching and fees for tuition.

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 64
title: Public School Law of Louisville - 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 64
summary: This statute mandates the segregation of public schools in Louisville, prohibiting children of the African race from attending schools with white children. It also requires that school taxes paid by individuals of the African race be kept separate and used exclusively for the education of children of the African race residing within the city or paying school taxes there.

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 70
title: Public School Law of Louisville - 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 70
summary: This statute outlines the organization and funding of public schools in Louisville, Kentucky. It designates cities or towns that maintain adequate, free common schools as a single district, entitled to a proportion of the school fund. These districts are to report to the County Commissioner and take a census of white children. The schools are governed by local authorities, and the Commissioner has no control over them. The statute also details the process for paying teachers and penalties for non-payment.

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 74
title: Public School Law of Louisville - 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 74
summary: This act amends a previous law concerning public schools in Louisville. It directs that a portion of school revenues, previously intended for the sinking fund, shall be used by the Louisville School Board to construct and equip three schoolhouses specifically for colored children, located in the eastern, western, and central parts of the city. These schools and their operations will be under the School Board's control. Any remaining funds after building the houses will be invested for the benefit of colored schools, with the interest exclusively applied to paying teachers and for maintenance and operation.

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 75
title: Public School Law of Louisv- 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 75
summary: This statute outlines the process for the Superintendent of Public Instruction to estimate and apportion school funds. It specifies that the pro rata share of revenue for each child is calculated based on the number of 'white children' between the ages of six and twenty. The statute also details the use of census returns or tax books for apportionment and the reporting requirements to the Auditor of Public Accounts and County Commissioners.

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 76
title: Public School Law of Louisville - 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 76
summary: This statute outlines provisions for public schools in cities and towns, including the establishment of a graded system of free schools and the levying of a special school tax. It also details the appointment and duties of School Commissioners for each county and the City of Louisville, requiring them to report the census of white children between the ages of six and twenty.

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 91
title: Public School Law of Louisv- 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 91
summary: This act levies an additional two-cent tax per $100 of property to equalize per capita funding for white and colored pupil children. It also repeals the capitation tax on colored people for common school purposes and explicitly prohibits white children from attending colored schools and vice versa, mandating separate schools for each race.

statute_citation: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 92
title: Public School Law of Louisville - 1882
citations: Public School Laws of the City of Louisville, 1882, p. 92
summary: This act proposes an additional tax of three cents per $100 worth of property to increase the common school fund and equalize the per capita funding for white and colored students. The act's effectiveness is contingent on ratification by a majority of qualified voters in an August 1882 election. Section 8 states the act takes effect upon passage for the purpose of submitting the vote to the people, and Note 2 confirms it was ratified.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1015, pp. 426–427
title: AN ACT to authorize the board of councilmen of Frankfort to issue bouds for school purposes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1015, pp. 426–427
summary: This act authorizes the board of councilmen of Frankfort to issue bonds up to $10,000 for the purpose of procuring a suitable building, furniture, fixtures, and apparatus for the "colored public school" of the city. The bonds are to be sold at face value and the funds used for this specific school.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1033, pp. 477–487
title: AN ACT to provide for a registration of voters in the city of Louisville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1033, pp. 477–487
summary: This act establishes a board composed of the county judge, sheriff, and county court clerk of Jefferson County to appoint four citizens in each election precinct of Louisville to serve as judges, clerk, and sheriff of registration. Eligibility requires being a voter and a house-keeper in the precinct. The act also mentions provisions for when there are two distinct political parties.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1154, pp. 693–694
title: AN ACT for the benefit of common school districts numbers three, eleven, twenty-eight, thirty, thirty-one, forty-five, forty-nine, fifty-two, fifty-five, fifty-nine, white, and numbers eight, twelve, fourteen, colored, in Madison county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1154, pp. 693–694
summary: This act authorizes the Superintendent of Public Instruction to issue drafts for payments to common school districts in Madison County. It specifies separate amounts for white districts ($99.40) and colored districts ($77.00), to be paid from the common school fund. The payment to white districts includes a portion for unbonded interest on surplus bonds.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1162, pp. 714–720
title: AN ACT to provide for good roads in Todd county, and to regulate taxation in the same.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1162, pp. 714–720
summary: This act outlines the process for road contractors in Todd County, Kentucky. It details the execution of bonds, approval by the county judge, and payment procedures. Crucially, Section 8 mandates that the Todd County judge shall provide work on county roads or town streets for persons convicted of penal offenses who are required to work on roads or streets, or to work out fines. This provision allows for the use of convicted individuals, potentially including those from the Black community who were disproportionately convicted of offenses, for forced labor on public works, a common characteristic of Jim Crow era labor practices.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1201, pp. 797–801

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1201, pp. 797–801
summary: This act establishes the Kuttawa common school district and outlines its management, funding, and operational requirements. Notably, it specifies that instruction shall be provided to "all white children" between the ages of six and twenty years residing in the district without charge. It also defines voter qualifications for school board elections, explicitly including "all the white qualified voters" and certain tax-paying or child-rearing widows or maids, while generally qualifying voters based on age, citizenship, and taxpaying status, with an exception for sex.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1371, pp. 1087–1088
title: AN ACT to prevent idleness and vagrancy in Fleming county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1371, pp. 1087–1088
summary: This act amends existing statutes regarding vagrancy in Fleming County. It mandates that convicted vagrants be sentenced to hard labor for 50 to 100 days. Jailers are required to ensure convicted individuals work eight hours a day, with refusal leading to a bread and water diet. A provision is made for the dependents of convicted laborers, with a daily payment of twenty-five cents to be covered by the county or the beneficiary of the labor.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1393, pp. 1123–1187
title: AN ACT to revise the charter of the city of Paducah, and reduce into one the several acts relating there to.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1393, pp. 1123–1187
summary: This statute, from the Laws of Kentucky in 1884, outlines the powers and responsibilities of public school trustees in McCracken County. Specifically, section 5 mandates that the trustees shall "provide separate buildings and schools for education of white and black pupils."

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1431, pp. 1258–1261
title: AN ACT for the benefit of common school district number forty-three, in Graves county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1431, pp. 1258–1261
summary: This act incorporates common school district number forty-three in Graves county, specifically mentioning 'white persons living in said district' as part of the incorporated entity. It grants the trustees powers to govern the school and enforce rules.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1489, pp. 1350–1351
title: AN ACT to authorize the levy and collection of additional tax in aid of public schools in common school district number sixteen, Breckinridge county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1489, pp. 1350–1351
summary: This act authorizes the trustees of common school district number sixteen in Breckinridge County (Hardinsburg district) to levy an ad valorem tax of up to twenty cents per one hundred dollars of taxable property and a capitation tax of up to one dollar and fifty cents per person over twenty-one years old. Crucially, it specifies that 'only white persons and property belonging to white persons shall be taxed.' The trustees are required to declare the tax amount annually by May 1st.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1518, pp. 1392–1393
title: AN ACT creating an additional voting place in the fourth magisterial district, of Fayette county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1518, pp. 1392–1393
summary: This act establishes an additional voting place in Fayette County's fourth magisterial district, designating the Bell school-house as polling place number two. It mandates that voters residing east of the Louisville, Cincinnati, and Lexington Railroad must vote at polling place number one, and those west of the railroad must vote at polling place number two. The sheriff is required to post notices informing voters of this division.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1536, p. 1416

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1536, p. 1416
summary: This act prohibits the sale or gifting of spirituous, vinous, or malt liquors within common school district number thirty in Graves county. Violators face fines. Notably, Section 4 specifies that if persons of color violate the act, the fines shall be appropriated to the benefit of the colored school in said district.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1595, pp. 1477–1478
title: AN ACT to authorize the trustees of common school district number one, in Grayson county, to levy and collect a tax for the benefit of the common school property in said district.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 1595, pp. 1477–1478
summary: This act authorizes the trustees of common school district number one in Grayson county to levy and collect an ad valorem tax for the years 1884 and 1885. The tax is to be levied on all property in the district listed by white citizens for taxation, not exceeding fifteen cents on every one hundred dollars worth of taxable property.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 822, pp. 69–72
title: AN ACT to organize and establish a system of common and graded schools in the town of Dover, and in common school district number two, in Mason county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 822, pp. 69–72
summary: This act establishes the Dover Graded School District and outlines the governance and operation of its schools. It specifies that the schools shall be taught for ten months each year and that every white child within the district, within the common school age, shall have free access and the right to attend free of charge.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 825, pp. 78–84
title: AN ACT for the benefit of Webster and Hopkins counties, relating to the public roads in said counties.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 825, pp. 78–84
summary: This statute outlines the use of convicted individuals and delinquent taxpayers for labor on county roads and streets. It allows county judges to assign work to those convicted of penal offenses, including working off fines, and to use restraints like ball and chains to prevent escape. It also mandates that delinquent capitation taxpayers in Webster County work off their taxes on roads, with surveyors authorized to collect taxes or oversee the work. Penalties are imposed for non-compliance.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 868, p. 142
title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to provide for the payment of debts contracted in building and furnishing a school-house, and for main. tain inga school in district number one, in Pendleton county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 868, p. 142
summary: This act amends a previous law concerning school funding in Pendleton County. It exempts colored persons and their property from the capitation and property taxes authorized by the original act for school purposes.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 961, pp. 352–354
title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the Owenton High School, in Owen county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 961, pp. 352–354
summary: This act amends the charter of the Owenton High School. It allows the school board to issue bonds for purchasing a new site, building, or repairing the school. It also states that the school shall be for whites only and that the question of a tax for the school will be submitted to voters.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 994, p. 394

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Local and Private Acts], 1884, ch. 994, p. 394
summary: This act amends the charter of the South Carrollton Male and Female Academy. It specifies that the election of trustees will be held by 'white male voters' of the common school district. The trustees will serve until their successors are elected and qualified.

statute_citation: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 51
title: Common School Laws - Article XII - Colored Schools
citations: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 51
summary: This article outlines the legal framework for the establishment and operation of separate schools for colored children in Kentucky. It details the disposition of funds for colored schools, the process of laying off school districts, the age and census requirements for colored pupils, and the election of trustees for colored schools. Crucially, it includes provisions that explicitly prohibit inter-racial attendance in common schools and prevent taxation or services from one race benefiting the other's schools, as well as restricting voting rights for trustees.

statute_citation: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 52
title: Common School Laws - 1885
citations: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 52
summary: This section of the Common School Laws from 1885 explicitly mandates racial segregation in common schools. It prohibits white individuals from contributing to schools for colored children and vice versa, and forbids individuals of one race from voting for trustees of schools designated for the other race. Furthermore, it explicitly states that white children cannot attend schools for colored children, and colored children cannot attend schools for white children. It also outlines the organization of Teachers' Institutes and State Teachers' Associations for colored people.

statute_citation: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 55
title: Colored School Fund
citations: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 55
summary: This section of the Common School Laws from 1885 discusses the constitutionality of a separate common school fund for colored children, established by an act on February 23, 1874. The text states that this act is unconstitutional, citing the case of Dawson vs. Lee.

statute_citation: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 7
title: AN ACT TO AMEND AND REFORM THE COMMON SCHOOL LAWS OF THIS COMMONWEALTH
citations: The Common School Laws of Kentucky, 1885, p. 7
summary: This act establishes a uniform system of common schools throughout Kentucky, outlining the structure, funding, and administration of the school system. It covers various aspects including the school fund, county taxation, boards of education, superintendents, districts, trustees, teachers, institutes, libraries, and fines. Notably, it includes a section specifically titled 'COLORED SCHOOLS'.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1001, pp. 541–543
title: AN ACT fixing the boundary and for the benefit of the school district No. 67, in Fleming county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1001, pp. 541–543
summary: This act establishes a new school district and outlines the process for electing trustees, listing children of school age, and voting on taxes for school construction. Notably, it specifies that lists of property owners and tithes for taxation purposes shall be made for 'all the white owners of property' and 'all the white tithes residing in said district.' Additionally, it allows for a per capita tax on 'each white male person of twenty-one years of age residing in said district.'

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1010, pp. 549–551
title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to incorporate Carr Institute."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1010, pp. 549–551
summary: This act amends the charter of the Carr Institute, a school, by detailing fees for tax collection and establishing liens for taxes. Crucially, it explicitly states that the provisions of this act shall only apply to the white population of the Fulton school district.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1094, pp. 661–665

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1094, pp. 661–665

It details the powers of the board, membership conditions, and benefit limits. Crucially, Section 8 explicitly states that only 'free-born white men between the ages of eighteen and forty-five' are eligible for membership.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1142, p. 717

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1142, p. 717
summary: This act authorizes the city of Lexington to issue bonds up to $30,000 for school purposes. The funds are to be used for purchasing land and erecting schoolhouses for both white and colored children, with the determination of the number of schoolhouses for colored children left to the discretion of the general council.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1173, pp. 756–757
title: AN ACT to consolidate common school districts numbered eighty—three (83), eighty-four(84) and eighty-six (86), for white children, in Barren county, Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 1173, pp. 756–757
summary: This act consolidates three common school districts (83, 84, and 86) specifically for white children in Barren County, Kentucky, into a single district. It outlines the process for electing trustees and states that the common school laws of the Commonwealth will apply to this consolidated district.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 685, pp. 41–47
title: AN ACT to establish a system of public graded schools in district No. 47, East Point.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 685, pp. 41–47
summary: This act establishes a public graded school system for district No. 47 in East Point, Kentucky. It explicitly states that the school affairs for white children of pupil age will be under the control and management of five trustees, elected by qualified white voters. It also defines who qualifies as a voter, including white widows, aliens who are taxpayers, or those with children to be educated between the ages of six and twenty.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 725, pp. 94–111
title: AN ACT to provide for there-organization, maintenance and supervising of common schools in the town of Louisa and vic in itv.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 725, pp. 94–111
summary: This act establishes a common school in a specific district in Louisa, Kentucky. It outlines the boundaries of the district, the duration of the school year (5-10 months), and specifies that 'all white children between the ages of six and twenty residing therein shall receive instruction without any charge therefor.' The management and control of the school and its funds are vested in a board of education whose members must possess the qualifications of 'white voters of said district.' Elections for the board are to be held annually, and only 'white qualified voters, and any maid or widow who is a tax payer' are eligible to vote.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 885, pp. 341–342
title: AN ACT for the benefit of colored common schools of Floyd county, and to authorize the superintendent and board of examiners of common schools of said county " to issue special license to persons to teach colored common schools of said county."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 885, pp. 341–342
summary: This act addresses the difficulty in finding qualified teachers for colored common schools in Floyd County. It authorizes the superintendent and board of examiners to issue special licenses to individuals to teach these schools, acknowledging that there were no local colored teachers who could obtain certificates under the existing rigid examination requirements. The preamble states the importance of these schools for the cultural development and civic duties of colored citizens.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 929, pp. 405–410
title: AN ACT to consolidate common school districts Nos.1 and 26, in Carrollcounty, and to provide for a school building and the better organ i zationof the public schools in said consolidated district.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 929, pp. 405–410
summary: This act allows the board of trustees of a school district in Ballard County to issue bonds, not exceeding $8,000, to fund the purchase of grounds, erection of buildings, and furnishing of school facilities. Crucially, it specifies that these facilities must be 'amply sufficient for the proper accommodation of all the white children of pupil age within the district thereby created.'

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 931, pp. 412–415
title: AN ACT to incorporate the Little Mount Cemetery Company, in Spencer county.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 931, pp. 412–415
summary: This act incorporates the Scaville and Lawrenceburg Turnpike Road Company. It also contains provisions for a cemetery board that has the power to segregate burial plots by race, confining 'colored people to one portion and white people to another'.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 974, p. 495
title: AN ACT to amend the charter of the city of Hawesville in relation too schools.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 974, p. 495
summary: This act mandates that funds received by the Hawesville board of education from licenses set aside for school purposes be divided equally between white and colored schools. The treasurer is required to distribute these funds proportionally based on the school census, paying the colored school trustees their share. statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 992, pp. 517–526

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1886, ch. 992, pp. 517–526
summary: This statute outlines procedures for challenging voter registration. It details how to serve notice to a registered voter, form a committee to hear evidence, and strike names from the register if deemed unlawfully registered. statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 795, pp. 710–715

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 795, pp. 710–715

It specifies that the tax will only take effect if approved by a majority of qualified white voters in the district. The election for this approval is to be ordered by the board of trustees, with specific notice requirements and voting procedures. The superintendent of common schools for Breckinridge county is to appoint election officers, or the board of trustees will if the superintendent fails to do so. The act also details the certification and delivery of poll books.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 837, pp. 787–788

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 837, pp. 787–788
summary: This act amends a previous law establishing public and high schools in Sebree, Kentucky. It allows for an election to be held to determine if the existing school law, which explicitly states it is for 'white children only,' should be put into full effect. The election process is detailed, including notice, voting procedures, and certification of results.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 839, p. 791

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 839, p. 791
summary: This act amends the law regarding the election of the county treasurer for Campbell County. statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 861, pp. 822–832

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 861, pp. 822–832
summary: This act amends a previous law regarding voter registration in Covington, Kentucky. Notably, it specifies that registration books should include a column for 'color'.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 869, pp. 846–847
title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled "An act to consolidate common school districts Nos.1 and 26, in Carroll county, and to provide for a school building and a better organization of the public schools in said consolidated district," approved May 7,1886; and providing for the levying of an additional…

The act also addresses existing debt for a school building and a previously levied tax to pay it off.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 896, pp. 903–906

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 896, pp. 903–906

The statute also outlines the institute's governance structure, including a board of trustees and other officers.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 905, pp. 929–937

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 905, pp. 929–937

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 928, pp. 968–1036

The statute mandates the delivery of registration and poll books to election officials and states that a person's vote will not be received unless their name is on the register or a certificate is produced.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 969, p. 1123

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, p. 407
title: AN ACT to incorporate and establish a system of public schools in district No. 49, including the town of Adairville.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, p. 407
summary: This act incorporates common school district No. 49, including the town of Adairville, into a school district under the control and management of trustees selected by the legal white voters within its limits. statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, p. 408

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, p. 408
summary: This act establishes a public school in Adairville and outlines the powers and duties of its board of trustees. Crucially, it explicitly states that only white children are eligible for admission to the school.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, p. 409

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2 [Private Acts], 1888, p. 409
summary: This act amends a previous act concerning public schools in Adairville. The taxes are to be levied on the first Saturday in April and due on the first day of September, collected by a board-appointed collector.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1008, pp. 56–63

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1101, pp. 251–253

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1105, pp. 257–263

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1106, pp. 263–272

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1162, pp. 376–377

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1236, pp. 483–484

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1236, pp. 483–484

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1265, pp. 530–531

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1273, pp. 546–553

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1273, pp. 546–553

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1331, p. 641

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1331, p. 641
summary: This act amends a previous law concerning public schools in Owensboro. It specifically states that the public school system is for 'white children' and outlines procedures for the expulsion of trustees who disturb the schools or abuse teachers. The amendment focuses on the governance and conduct within the school board and its officials, but the explicit mention of 'white children' in the context of public education is a strong indicator of racial segregation.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1342, pp. 648–657
title: AN ACT to provide for the election and in part to define the duties of a mayor, board of councilmen and school trustees of the city of Frankfort, and to provide for the establishment of a board of commissioners to control the police and fire departments thereof, and to define their duties.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1342, pp. 648–657
summary: This statute mandates the creation of registration books for voters in Frankfort. These books must include columns for the voter's name, residence, color, and the election for which they are registered. Registration is to be conducted alphabetically. The statute explicitly requires a column for 'color' and states that the list of voters shall show 'whether he be white or colored.' This explicit racial categorization in the voter registration process is a hallmark of Jim Crow laws designed to disenfranchise Black voters.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1514, p. 903

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1514, p. 903
summary: This act amends a previous act that established public and high schools in Sebree, Kentucky, specifically for white children. The amendment strikes out the first section and inserts a new one, but the core intent of racial segregation in education remains. The new section reiterates the establishment of the Sebree Public and High Schools.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1515, pp. 904–905

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 3 [Private Acts], 1888, ch. 1515, pp. 904–905

Crucially, it includes a provision stating that 'No colored person shall pay any of the tax named in said act or in this act.' statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 114, pp. 482–484

Further taxes can be imposed for school furniture, insurance, repairs, census taking, elections, janitors, fuel, and incidental expenses, also levied on property belonging to and controlled by 'white persons'. Additionally, patrons of the school are to be taxed to cover coal and incidental expenses.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 126, pp. 496–500

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 190, pp. 585–586

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 201, pp. 612–624

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 201, pp. 612–624
summary: This act details the process for voter registration in Danville, Kentucky. statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 205, p. 632

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 205, p. 632

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 206, pp. 633–634

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 250, pp. 737–739
title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to establish a system of public graded schools in the city of Somerset, Kentucky."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 250, pp. 737–739
summary: This act amends an existing law concerning the school district of Somerset, Kentucky. It authorizes the board of trustees to levy an ad valorem tax and issue bonds for school purposes. Crucially, it grants the trustees the power to adopt the assessment of the city assessor of Somerset for property belonging to "white persons" within the city limits. This implies a separate assessment or differential treatment for property not belonging to white persons, which is a strong indicator of racial segregation in the context of Jim Crow era legislation.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 266, pp. 773–801
title: AN ACT to amend an act, entitled"An act to regulate municipal elections in the city of Louisville."
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 266, pp. 773–801
summary: This statute outlines procedures for voters who are unable to read, requiring them to make an affidavit to receive assistance in marking their ballot. The affidavit process involves the voter affirming their inability to read and the election clerk then marking the ballot on their behalf. This provision, while seemingly neutral, was historically used to disenfranchise Black voters by creating a barrier to voting that disproportionately affected them due to lower literacy rates resulting from systemic discrimination.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 327, pp. 905–916

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 327, pp. 905–916
summary: This section of the Laws of Kentucky from 1890 outlines the election process for city officials. Specifically, Section 6 details the qualifications for voting in city elections. This requirement for tax payment as a prerequisite for voting is a common feature of Jim Crow-era disenfranchisement tactics, often disproportionately affecting Black citizens.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 372, pp. 1015–1025

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 495, pp. 1384–1394

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 497, pp. 97–100

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 497, pp. 97–100

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 508, pp. 1416–1424

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 53, pp. 390–392

summary: This act allows the trustees of Hickman College to submit a question to the legally qualified white voters of Hickman City regarding a $3,000 subscription by taxation to complete and furnish the college building and improve its grounds. statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 1, 1890, ch. 96, pp. 455–456

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, v. 2, 1890, ch. 1003, pp. 1327–1343
