statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 1136
title: Separate Coach Law Application to Sleeping Cars
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 1136
summary: This statute discusses the application of Kentucky's separate coach law (Ky. Stats., Sec. 795) to sleeping cars. It clarifies that a sleeping car owned and operated by a Pullman Car Company, even when attached to a defendant company's passenger train, is not considered 'operated' by the defendant company under the separate coach law. Therefore, the defendant company is not liable for hauling a sleeping car without separate compartments or for failing to ensure a colored passenger in such a sleeper entered the day coach compartment set aside for their race, especially when the passenger had purchased a ticket entitling them to ride in the sleeper.

statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 191
title: FREIGHT TRAIN
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 191
summary: This statute addresses the application of separate coach requirements for white and colored passengers on freight trains. It states that Kentucky Statutes, Section 795, requiring separate coaches for white and colored passengers, does not apply to passengers in a caboose car attached to a freight train. The case discussed involved a defendant who sold tickets to both white and colored passengers for a caboose car on a branch line, with no separate compartments or signs. The court ruled that the caboose car on a freight train, even if carrying passengers, was exempt from the separate compartment requirement.

statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 262
title: GRADED SCHOOL DISTRICT
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 262
summary: This entry discusses graded school districts in Kentucky. It explicitly states that 'colored graded schools did not exist' when certain statutes were enacted in 1906, implying that these statutes were originally intended for white common schools. However, it also asserts that the terms 'graded school district' and 'common school district' were intended to be synonymous and interchangeable, suggesting that the existing legal framework for graded schools could be applied to colored schools. This indicates a legal interpretation that allowed for the application of graded school structures to separate educational systems for Black students, even if not explicitly named in the original legislation.

statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 372
title: IDENTITY
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 372
summary: This entry discusses the legal concept of 'identity' in various contexts, including ticket purchasers and money identification. Crucially, it references a statute (Ky. Stat., 796) and court cases (L. & N. R. Co. v. Com.) that address 'substantial equality of accommodations' for white and colored passengers, stating that equality does not mean identity. This implies a legal framework for separate but supposedly equal facilities.

statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 618
title: KNOWINGLY
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 618
summary: This entry defines the legal term 'knowingly' and provides examples of its application in Kentucky case law. One example specifically addresses a railroad company's violation of a statute requiring signs to indicate the race for which compartments on interurban cars were designated. The court presumed the violation was knowing and willful if the signs were absent.

statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 686
title: Legitimacy of Children in Kentucky
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 686
summary: This statute addresses the legitimacy of children born from various marriage circumstances in Kentucky. It specifically states that the issue of a marriage between a white person and a negro or mulatto shall not be legitimate. It also outlines conditions under which children from void marriages, marriages contracted in good faith with a presumed-dead spouse, or customary marriages of negroes and mulattoes prior to February 14, 1866, would be considered legitimate. The statute also details provisions for legitimizing children through subsequent marriage and recognition by the father.

statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 935
title: MULATTO
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 935
summary: This entry defines a 'mulatto' in the context of statutes that do not specifically define the term. It cites a case (Gentry v. McMinnis) that held a mulatto to be a person with at least one-fourth African blood. This definition is relevant to understanding racial classifications used in historical statutes, which often underpinned Jim Crow laws.

statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 938
title: An Act entitled " an Act for the benefit of Belle Point,"
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 2, 1916, p. 938
summary: This statute describes an unconstitutional act that levied a tax on white citizens of a town to fund an additional five months of school. While white children within the town could attend for free, children residing outside the town limits but within the district were also allowed to attend free for the initial five months, but would have to pay tuition thereafter. The court found this unconstitutional because it taxed the town to educate the entire district.

statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 3, 1916, p. 1193
title: WHITE PERSON - Taxation for Graded School Purposes
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 3, 1916, p. 1193
summary: This entry discusses the taxation of property for graded school purposes. It states that a corporation's property is taxable under a statute authorizing taxation of 'white persons' for such purposes, unless the corporation can prove its corporators and stockholders are Black. The intent is for the burden to fall on all property within the district except that of Black individuals.

statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 3, 1916, p. 261
title: PROPERTY TAX 2720 PROPS
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 3, 1916, p. 261
summary: This entry from The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary (1916) states that the right to teach white and negro children in a private school at the same time and place is not a property right, citing Berea College v. Com. This implies a legal framework that would prevent integrated education, a hallmark of Jim Crow laws.

statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 3, 1916, p. 621
title: SEGREGATION
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 3, 1916, p. 621
summary: This entry defines segregation in the context of Louisville's municipal segregation ordinance. It states that the ordinance was a valid exercise of police power, deemed reasonable and expedient for public welfare. The purpose was to prevent violence stemming from racial antipathies and to preserve racial solidarity. It also references a note on the validity of segregation statutes or ordinances prohibiting persons of different races or colors from living in the same locality.

statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 3, 1916, p. 642
title: Separate Coach Law
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 3, 1916, p. 642
summary: This statute, known as the "Separate Coach Law" (Ky. Stats., Secs. 795 and 796), mandates that railroad companies operating in Kentucky must provide separate coaches or cars for white and colored passengers. It specifies that compartments divided by a partition with a door will be considered separate coaches, and each must be clearly marked to indicate the race for which it is designated. The law also prohibits discrimination in the quality, convenience, or accommodations provided for white and colored passengers, stating that substantial equality, not identical accommodations, is required.

statute_citation: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 3, 1916, p. 643
title: The Separate Coach Law
citations: The Kentucky Judicial Dictionary 3, 1916, p. 643
summary: This entry discusses the constitutionality and application of Kentucky's Separate Coach Law, which mandated separate railway cars for white and colored passengers. It states that the law applies equally to both races and that colored passengers are entitled to the same redress as white passengers for violations. The entry also notes that the conductor, not the railroad company, is liable for failure to assign passengers to their designated coaches.

Crucially, it mandates the segregation of white and colored races within these institutions. The statute also addresses the financial responsibilities of counties for transporting and maintaining committed girls, as well as the payment of expenses and salaries for the institution from the State treasury.

The statute also details the compensation of the superintendent, the process for employing architects, purchasing materials, and the selection and size of the farm.

statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4399a-3
title: § 4399a-3. Election of county superintendent.
citations: The Kentucky Statutes, Fifth Edition, v. 3, 1918, § 4399a-3, p. 1125

It mandates that such a superintendent must be a resident of the county outside of the city or town. It also lists other county officials and teachers who are ineligible to hold the office of county superintendent. The statute further details the election process, term of office, and bond requirements for county superintendents. A key provision states that in counties with separate school systems in cities of the first or second class, the county superintendent must reside outside such cities and be elected by voters residing outside those cities.

statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4420a-3
title: § 4420a-3. White and colored school districts.

It explicitly states that the provisions of the law do not apply to colored school districts. However, it mandates that taxes collected from railroad and bridge companies in white graded or common school subdistricts shall be apportioned and distributed between the white school district and any colored common school district located over the same boundary. The distribution ratio is based on the proportion of white children of pupil age and colored children of pupil age residing in the district or subdistrict.

statute_citation: Ky. Stat. § 4468a-3

Specifically, it mandates that railroad and bridge taxes collected for the benefit of a white graded common school district or white common school sub-district should be distributed between that white district and any colored common school district if their boundaries are the same. title: AN ACT to amend chapter 146 of an Act of the General Assembly passed at its 1920 session entitled " An Act relating to free public libraries in cities and towns of the third, fourth, fifth and sixth classes of this Commonwealth ", the same being sections 2741d -1 to and including 2741d -5 of…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, ch. 94, pp. 496–500
summary: This act amends existing legislation concerning free public libraries in cities and towns of certain classes. It also outlines the taxation of separate property of the two races and the division of funds derived from such taxation.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, p. 456
title: An Act to Amend Section 148.270 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes, Relating to Voter Registration
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1932, p. 456
summary: This statute outlines the requirements for voter registration in Kentucky, including the collection of personal information such as name, address, color or race, sex, physical characteristics, party affiliation, occupation, birthplace, age, length of residency, naturalization status, and other means of identification. It also details procedures for voters who are unable to write their names, requiring them to make a mark attested by the clerk after an investigation and oath.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1934, ch. 155, pp. 738–773
title: AN ACT to reorganize and simplify the executive department of the state government for the purpose of providing for better service and economy, through the enactment of an administrative code providing for the administrative departments and independent agencies therein specified; redistributing the…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1934, ch. 155, pp. 738–773
summary: This statute establishes the Department of Education, consolidating various educational bodies. It explicitly mentions "State institutions of higher education for negroes" and abolishes the "Board of Trustees of Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons" and "Board of Trustees of West Kentucky Industrial College." This indicates a system of segregated higher education for Black individuals.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1934, ch. 65, pp. 256–406
title: AN ACT providing for a more uniform and efficient system of public schools and colleges throughout the Commonwealth of Kentucky, repealing section 4363 to section 4376b -10 inclusive, and section 4378 to section 4399, inclusive, Baldwin's 1930 Revision of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes with the 1933…

summary: This statute consolidates and revises various sections of Baldwin's 1930 Revision of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes concerning public education. It specifically includes provisions for the 'public education for colored children' and 'higher education for colored persons', indicating a racially segregated educational system.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1934, ch. 97, p. 485
title: AN ACT to authorize the State Librarian to furnish without cost to the Library of the University of Kentucky and to the libraries of the four State Teachers Colleges, certain public documents and books when authorized by the trustees to do 80.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1934, ch. 97, p. 485
summary: This act authorizes the State Librarian to provide public documents, books, and manuscripts from the State Library, free of charge, to the University of Kentucky Library and the libraries of the four state teachers colleges, as well as the two colored teachers colleges. The decision to furnish these materials rests with the trustees of the State Library.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 19, pp. 71–77
title: § 19. State Department of Education.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 19, pp. 71–77
summary: This statute appropriates funds for various educational purposes, including teacher training, vocational agriculture and home economics, vocational rehabilitation, and specifically allocates funds for the maintenance and operation of the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons. It also designates fees and receipts from the boarding, rooming, and athletic departments of this college to a revolving fund.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 20, pp. 77–78
title: § 20. Kentucky Institution for the Education of the Blind.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 20, pp. 77–78
summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky School for the Blind for the fiscal years ending June 30, 1935, and June 30, 1936. It explicitly allocates separate funding for the 'White Department' and the 'Colored Department' of the school.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 21, p. 78
title: § 21. Kentucky School for the Deaf.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 21, p. 78
summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky School for the Deaf, specifically allocating separate amounts for a 'White Department' and a 'Department for Colored Children'. It also appropriates funds for Morehead State Teachers College.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 26, pp. 84–91
title: § 26. University of Kentucky.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 26, pp. 84–91
summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky Children's Home Society for White Children and the Kentucky Children's Home Society for Colored Children for the fiscal years ending June 30, 1935, and June 30, 1936. The society for white children receives $100,000.00 for each year, while the society for colored children receives $25,000.00 for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1935, with the appropriation for the following year being cut off in the provided text.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 29, pp. 92–99
title: § 29. Department of Insurance.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1934, § 29, pp. 92–99
summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Colored Red Cross Hospital in Louisville for the fiscal years ending June 30, 1935, and June 30, 1936. It also appropriates funds for the Home for Incurables and the Department of Insurance.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1936, ch. 42, pp. 184–187
title: AN ACT amending Section three (3) of Article five (5) of Chapter sixty -five (65) of the Acts of the General Assembly of nineteen thirty -four (1934), being Section four thousand three hundred ninety -nine -three (4399-3), Kentucky Statutes, Baldwin's Kentucky Statutes Service of nineteen thirty…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1936, ch. 42, pp. 184–187
summary: This statute amends existing law regarding independent school districts. It specifies that independent school districts embracing cities of the first five classes, along with their surrounding territories, and any independent graded common school districts with a census of 250 or more white children, will be designated as independent school districts. It also sets a condition for continued operation: districts (other than those in cities of the first five classes already operating as independent districts) must maintain a census of at least 250 white children, unless the State Board of Education determines that operating as an independent district allows for a more efficient school service program.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1936, ch. 43, pp. 187–189
title: AN ACT to provide State aid for education in certain courses of study of State students pursuing certain courses of study at educational institutions outside of the State for whom no such courses are provided in the educational institutions of the State, and prescribing the conditions under which…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1936, ch. 43, pp. 187–189
summary: This act provides for the payment of tuition and fees by the Commonwealth of Kentucky for residents who are qualified to study at the University of Kentucky or other state institutions but cannot due to Section 187 of the Kentucky Constitution. These individuals are permitted to pursue such courses at educational institutions outside of the state, and their expenses will be covered. The State Superintendent of Public Instruction will ascertain and pay these tuition and fees, with the State Board of Education prescribing rules and regulations. Funds are appropriated for this purpose, with a limit of $175.00 per person per school year.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1936, ch. 45, pp. 191–212
title: AN ACT relating to suffrage and elections and providing a method of registering voters of this Commonwealth residing outside of the corporate limits of cities of the first class, fixing penalties for violations of this Act and repealing Chapter sixty-four (64) of the Acts of the General Assembly…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1936, ch. 45, pp. 191–212
summary: This statute details the information required on voter registration cards, including fields for 'Color'. While not explicitly discriminatory on its face, the inclusion of a 'Color' field in voter registration forms during the Jim Crow era was a common mechanism for enforcing segregation and disenfranchisement of Black voters.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 40
title: Appropriations for Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons and West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 40
summary: This statute appropriates funds for the operation and maintenance of two institutions specifically designated for "Colored Persons": the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons and the West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons. It outlines specific amounts for salaries, expenses, materials, repairs, boarding, rooming, athletics, student activities, and instructional equipment for both colleges. It also details how fees and other operating receipts will be handled for the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 41
title: Appropriations for Institutions of Higher Learning and Schools for the Blind
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 41
summary: This statute appropriates funds for various educational institutions. Notably, it allocates $5,000.00 to pay the college tuition of negro students required to go out of state for higher education. It also details separate appropriations for the 'White Department' and 'Colored Department' of the Kentucky School for the Blind, with significantly different funding levels ($61,500.00 for the White Department and $7,000.00 for the Colored Department).

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 42
title: Appropriations for Kentucky School for the Deaf and Department of Education
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 42
summary: This statute appropriates funds for the operation of the Kentucky School for the Deaf, specifically allocating $110,000.00 for the 'White Department' and $8,500.00 for the 'Department for Colored Children'. It also appropriates funds for the Department of Education for common schools, textbook purchases, and operational expenses.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 43
title: Appropriations for Educational Institutions
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 43
summary: This statute appropriates funds for various educational purposes, including vocational education, vocational rehabilitation, the State Board of Education, the Division of Certification, the State Textbook Commission, the War Orphans' Fund, and specifically allocates $62,000.00 for the Kentucky State Industrial College for Colored Persons, along with an additional $3,000.00 for materials and repairs, and funds for boarding, rooming, athletics, and student activities.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 44
title: Appropriations for Educational Institutions
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 44
summary: This statute appropriates funds for the West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons and also allocates funds to pay the college tuition of negro students required to seek higher education outside of the state. It also details the funding mechanisms for the institution through fees and operating receipts.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 45
title: Acts of the General Assembly, 1936 - Institution for the Blind and School for the Deaf Funding
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 45
summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Kentucky School for the Blind, specifically allocating $61,500.00 for the 'White Department' and $7,000.00 for the 'Colored Department'. It also appropriates funds for a workshop for adult blind and the 'White Department' of the Kentucky School for the Deaf ($110,000.00).

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 46
title: Chapter 133 - Department for Colored Children and Morehead State Teachers College Appropriations
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 46
summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Department for Colored Children and for the maintenance and operation of Morehead State Teachers College. Specifically, it allocates $8,500.00 for the Department for Colored Children and $180,000.00 for Morehead State Teachers College for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1937, covering various operational expenses. It also details funding for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1938, for the college.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 57
title: Appropriations for Charitable Institutions, 1936
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 57
summary: This statute appropriates funds for various institutions and societies in Kentucky for the fiscal year ending June 30, 1938. Notably, it allocates specific sums for the 'Kentucky Children's Home Society for Colored Children' and the 'Colored Bed Cross Hospital, at Louisville', indicating a segregated approach to the distribution of public funds for charitable purposes.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 59
title: Appropriations for State Institutions
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Extraordinary Session, 1936, p. 59
summary: This statute details appropriations for various state institutions, including specific allocations for the Kentucky Children's Home Society for White Children and the Kentucky Children's Home Society for Colored Children. It also includes funds for hospitals for the insane, feeble-minded, and epileptic wards of the state, and for cooperation with the Federal Government under the Social Security Act.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 111, pp. 629–651
title: AN ACT relating to primary and general elections and providing for a State -wide purgation of the registration lists of voters in the Commonwealth of Kentucky and providing for a Statewide registration and purgation board, and creating a county registration and purgation board for each of the…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 111, pp. 629–651
summary: This statute establishes a County Board of Registration and Purgation in each county of the Commonwealth of Kentucky. The board is appointed by the State Board of Registration and Purgation and consists of three members. Two members are chosen from the two dominant political parties, and one is selected by the State Board. Members must be at least twenty-one years old, reside in the county, and possess the qualifications of a legal voter. The State Board can remove members at its discretion.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 12, pp. 1092–1093
title: AN ACT to provide approved high school service for all pupils.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 12, pp. 1092–1093
summary: This act mandates that county and independent school boards provide approved high school education for all children of high school grade residing within their districts. It allows for maintaining schools or contracting with other districts. A key provision states that if the number of pupils of either race is insufficient to maintain a high school, the board must make provisions for them.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 147, pp. 772–774
title: AN ACT amending Chapter forty -two (42) of the Acts of the General Assembly of nineteen thirty -six (1936), being Section four thousand three hundred ninety-nine -three (4399-3), Carroll's Kentucky Statute, 1936 edition relating to independent school districts.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 147, pp. 772–774
summary: This act redefines independent graded common school districts, requiring a minimum of 200 white children in the school census enumeration for a district to continue operating as independent, with exceptions for certain city classes and temporary allowances by the State Board of Education. The State Board of Education has final decision-making power regarding temporary operational status.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 15, pp. 1097–1099
title: AN ACT providing for the purchase of property in Paintsville Kentucky, known as " The Mayo College property ", and for the establishment thereon of a State Vocational School; providing for the maintenance and operation of said school, and making appropriations therefor.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 15, pp. 1097–1099
summary: This act authorizes the purchase of the "Mayo College property" in Paintsville, Kentucky, for the establishment of a State Vocational School. Section 2 explicitly states that the Mayo State Vocational School is established and maintained 'for white persons'.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 1, pp. 1022–1051
title: AN ACT providing a Teachers Retirement System for the State of Kentucky; providing for retirement allowances for teachers of State supported Colleges, Public Schools, (including all elementary and secondary schools of the state); providing for disability benefits for disabled teachers of such…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 1, pp. 1022–1051; Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 1, pp. 54–100
summary: This act defines terms related to the Teachers' Retirement System, including 'Present Teacher' and 'New Teacher'. It specifically mentions the 'West Kentucky Industrial College for Colored Persons at Frankfort, Kentucky' as an institution whose teachers engaged in classroom instruction are eligible for the state retirement system. This explicit mention of a college for 'Colored Persons' within the context of a state-wide retirement system suggests a segregated educational system, a hallmark of Jim Crow era legislation.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 20, pp. 1105–1111
title: AN ACT providing for matrons for jails and station houses in cities of the first class; providing for their appointment, their duties, their removal, their compensation, and repealing Chapter 8 of the Acts of 1912 of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, now embraced in Sections…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 20, pp. 1105–1111
summary: This statute mandates that mayors of first-class cities designate specific station houses for the detention of female prisoners awaiting trial. It also requires the designation of the county jail for this purpose. Crucially, it mandates the appointment of two "respectable women" as matrons to supervise female prisoners. It then explicitly allows for the appointment of a "colored respectable woman" as an Assistant Police Matron. This provision, while seemingly about care, creates a racially segregated role within the correctional system.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 275, pp. 1007–1022
title: AN ACT repealing, amending and re -enacting Section 551, Kentucky Statutes, relating to corporations, their management and control, the election and qualifications of directors of corporations.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 275, pp. 1007–1022
summary: This proclamation from Governor A. B. Chandler, issued on March 2, 1938, convenes an extraordinary session of the Kentucky General Assembly. Among the stated purposes for the session are addressing inadequate provisions for vocational education for white people in Eastern Kentucky and for Negroes in Western Kentucky. This explicit mention of separate provisions based on race for vocational education strongly indicates a Jim Crow-era policy.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 29, pp. 1136–1144
title: AN ACT to amend and re -enact Sections 4527-59 to 4527-81, inclusive, of the Kentucky Statutes, Baldwin's 1936 Revision, relating to higher education for negroes; changing the name of the Kentucky State Industrial College to "Kentucky State College for Negroes "; discontinuing the West Kentucky…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1938, ch. 29, pp. 1136–1144
summary: This act amends sections of the Kentucky Statutes related to higher education for negroes. It specifically changes the name of the Kentucky State Industrial College to "Kentucky State College for Negroes".

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 106, pp. 482–485
title: AN ACT relating to libraries and library service, and to the powers, duties and functions of the Library Extension Division of the Department of Library and Archives.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 106, pp. 482–485
summary: This statute outlines the administration of federal grants for library service in Kentucky. It mandates that appointments to the Library Extension Division and participating libraries be based on merit and efficiency, without political consideration. Crucially, it requires the Library Extension Division to make plans to lessen inequalities of opportunity for library service and to make equitable apportionment of funds so as to provide library facilities to both the white and colored races. It also details the process of notifying the U.S. Commissioner of Education and entering into contracts for local public library service.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 125, pp. 553–562
title: AN ACT to amend Sections 3235b-l to 3236b-18, inclusive, of Car roll's Kentucky Statutes, 1936 Edition.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 125, pp. 553–562
summary: This act amends existing statutes concerning public parks in cities of the second class. It explicitly states that public parks established for the recreation, pleasure, and welfare of the 'white population' shall be managed by a 'Board of Park Commissioners (White)'. This indicates a legally mandated segregation of public park facilities based on race.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 16, pp. 166–222

summary: This statute appropriates funds for the Department of Welfare in Kentucky for the year 1940. statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 196, pp. 864–866
title: AN ACT to repeal section 4 of 1924 House Bill No. 44, which amended section 415b-9 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes, 1922 edition, relating to pensions for Confederate veterans, by amending section 415b-9 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes, 1936 edition, to read like section 415b-9 of Carroll's Kentucky…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, ch. 196, pp. 864–866
summary: This act re-enacts sections of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes concerning vagrancy. It grants circuit, police, quarterly, and justice courts jurisdiction over vagrancy offenses, with police, quarterly, and justice courts deemed always open for such trials. It also mandates sheriffs, constables, marshals, and policemen to watch for vagrants, warn them to leave and find work, and disperse groups of vagrants if necessary, using reasonable force.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, p. 863
title: Vagrancy Statute Re-enactment
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1940, p. 863
summary: This statute re-enacts and defines vagrancy for able-bodied males and females. It outlines conditions such as habitual loitering without means of support, refusal to engage in honest labor, desertion of family without support, and habitual refusal to work while loitering in public places. Penalties include fines and imprisonment, with increased penalties for subsequent offenses.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 1, pp. 56–113
title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation, maintenance, support and functioning of the State Government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, including each of the various officers, departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and sub -divisions of the State Government, and the purchase of record…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 1, pp. 56–113
summary: This statute details appropriations for various aspects of public education in Kentucky for the year 1942. It includes funding for general school expenses, textbooks, scholarships, vocational education, and specifically allocates funds for the 'Kentucky State College for Negroes' and the 'West Kentucky Vocational Training School' for Negroes, as well as 'College Tuition for Negroes' to attend institutions outside the state. It also lists appropriations for the 'Kentucky School for the Blind - White' and 'Kentucky School for the Blind - Colored'.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 31, pp. 276–277
title: AN ACT relating to the transfer of prisoners confined in any of the state penal institutions or reformatories.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 31, pp. 276–277
summary: This act charges the Commissioner of Welfare with classifying and segregating prisoners in state penal institutions and reformatories based on various factors including past records, rehabilitation potential, and influence on other prisoners. The Commissioner is also given the authority to transfer prisoners between institutions. The act declares an emergency and is effective upon passage.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 53, pp. 383–384
title: AN ACT relating to public parks in cities of the second class. Be it Enacted by the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky:
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 53, pp. 383–384
summary: This act consolidates and amends sections of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes concerning public parks in second-class cities. It allows cities to appropriate funds for park purchase, care, and improvement, and to maintain them from city funds. Crucially, it mandates the annual appropriation of two separate funds for park care and maintenance, one for a 'white park board' and the other for a 'colored park board', with funds paid out only upon order from the respective boards.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1942, ch. 87, pp. 539–540
title: AN ACT to amend section 125b - 1 of Carroll's Kentucky Statutes, 1936 edition, relating to the office of Commonwealth's Attorney in counties containing a population of one hundred and fifty thousand or more.

summary: This act amends a statute concerning the office of Commonwealth's Attorney in counties with a population of 150,000 or more. The act also addresses the increase in work and the need to increase the number of district detectives in these offices.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 131, pp. 301–309

Examinations are to be conducted by a commission, with notice published in the largest circulation newspaper. Applicants who served in the US military during wartime and received an honorable discharge receive a five percent increase in their examination grade. The commission certifies ranked lists of applicants to the fiscal court.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 1, pp. 472–524
title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation, maintenance, support and functioning of the State Government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, including each of the various offices, departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and subdivisions of the State Government, and the purchase of record…

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 52, pp. 148–150

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 52, pp. 148–150
summary: This statute amends Section 97.470 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes, 1942 Edition. It allows cities to appropriate funds for public parks and maintain them. statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 88, pp. 213–215

citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 88, pp. 213–215

Election officers must record these cases.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 97, pp. 223–228
title: AN ACT making provision for State Tuberculosis Sanatoria. Be it Enacted by the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky:
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1944, ch. 97, pp. 223–228
summary: This act outlines provisions for sanatoriums, including patient admission, transfer, and the specific requirement for sanatoriums to receive and provide adequate facilities for the treatment of paying and pauper patients of the negro race who are residents of the district. statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 147, pp. 463–466

summary: This act mandates the use of rubber stamps with the words "PURGATION RECOMMENDED" and a space for "Reason" and signatures of election judges. These stamps are to be provided to each precinct, except those within a first-class city, for use during primary elections. The purpose is to facilitate the process of recommending the purgation (removal) of voters from the rolls.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 160, pp. 502–503
title: AN ACT to amend Section 26.610 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes, relating to Matrons for Police Courts of Cities of the first class.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 160, pp. 502–503
summary: This act amends existing law to require two court matrons in cities of the first class: one white and one of the colored race. These matrons are responsible for investigating and reporting on women and girls awaiting trial, and supervising those under suspended sentence. Both matrons are to be paid the same salary.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 38, pp. 83–121
title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation, maintenance, support and functioning of the State Government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, including each of the various offices, departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and subdivisions of the State Government, and the purchase of record…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 38, pp. 83–121
summary: This section of the 1946 Acts of the General Assembly details appropriations for various state institutions and programs, including cancer control, tuberculosis sanatoria, and the Colored Red Cross Hospital. It also outlines funding for the Department of Welfare, including its various divisions.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 67, p. 174
title: AN ACT relating to higher education for Negroes.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1946, ch. 67, p. 174
summary: This act amends Section 166.170 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes concerning the granting of aid for higher education. It outlines the process for the State Board of Education to prescribe rules for aid, for the Superintendent of Public Instruction to ascertain and pay tuition and fees, and for prorating funds if insufficient. A maximum of $350.00 is allowed per person per school year.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 112, p. 313
title: AN ACT relating to education in fields related to health, with particular reference to the education of, and the training of nurses and doctors of the Negro race.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 112, p. 313
summary: This act allows hospitals to provide instruction in nursing, medicine, surgery, or other related graduate-level courses if their governing body elects to do so. It specifically addresses the lack of accredited training facilities for Negro women in nursing and postgraduate training for Negro doctors in Kentucky, while noting that adequate provisions exist for other races. The act aims to enable such training within hospitals that accept Negro patients.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 190, pp. 462–466
title: AN ACT relating to the state tuberculosis sanatoria, including Hazelwood Sanatorium; providing for a State Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission and transferring to such commission certain powers and duties now possessed by the State Board of Health, the Tuberculosis Sanatoria Commission of Kentucky and…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 190, pp. 462–466
summary: This act amends existing statutes concerning state tuberculosis sanatoria. It specifies provisions for paying and pauper patients, including the allocation of accommodations and the transfer of patients. Crucially, it mandates that provisions be made at each sanatorium for the receipt and furnishing of adequate facilities for the treatment of paying and pauper patients of the Negro race who are residents of the district. It also clarifies the cost of transporting patients.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 2, pp. 16–52
title: AN ACT appropriating money for the operation, maintenance, support and functioning of the State Government of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, including each of the various offices, departments, boards, commissions, institutions, and subdivisions of the State Government, excepting the State Road Fund…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1948, ch. 2, pp. 16–52
summary: This statute appropriates funds for the operation of various sanatoria and hospitals, including specific allocations for the Covington T.B. Sanatorium, Warren County T.B. Sanatorium, Kentucky Division of Women's Field Army of American Society for Control of Cancer, and the Colored Red Cross Hospital. It also allocates funds for Mental Hygiene and the Department of Welfare.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1952, ch. 134, pp. 342–378
title: AN ACT relating to qualification, registration and purgation of voters.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1952, ch. 134, pp. 342–378
summary: This statute outlines the compensation and meeting schedules for county boards of registration and purgation. It specifies daily pay rates for board members and secretaries, with different provisions for counties with and without cities of the first class. The statute also details the number of days the board must meet, particularly around election periods, and mandates that purgation be concluded at least twenty days before any primary or general election. Meetings are to be held at the courthouse unless otherwise necessary and with proper notice. It also includes a mechanism for citizens to prefer charges against a board that fails to meet or purge adequately.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1952, ch. 41, pp. 80–88
title: AN ACT relating to education.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1952, ch. 41, pp. 80–88
summary: This statute amends Section 166.040 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes to explicitly state that the purpose of the West Kentucky Vocational School is to provide vocational training facilities for colored children. It also amends Section 166.050 and 166.060 regarding the appointment and removal of the school's president and employees.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1954, ch. 2, pp. 24–25
title: AN ACT to amend and re-enact Section 145 of the Constitution of the Commonwealth of Kentucky. That upon the concurrence of three-fifths of all the members elected to each House of the General Assembly, the ayes and nays being taken thereon and entered in full in their respective journals, Section…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1954, ch. 2, pp. 24–25
summary: This act amends Section 145 of the Kentucky Constitution regarding voter qualifications and disenfranchisement. It outlines the general requirements for voting (age, residency) and then lists exceptions, including persons convicted of treason, felony, bribery in an election, or "such high misdemeanor as the general assembly may declare shall operate as an exclusion from the right of suffrage." It also notes that such excluded persons may be restored to civil rights by executive pardon.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1956, ch. 25, pp. 62–65
title: AN ACT relating to recreational facilities in cities of the second class.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1956, ch. 25, pp. 62–65
summary: This act repeals existing powers and duties granted to separate 'Board of Park Commissioners (White)' and 'Board of Park Commissioners (Colored)' in cities of the second class, vesting all such powers and duties in the city itself. This implies the consolidation of previously segregated park management structures.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Special Session, 1956, § 3, pp. 63–64
title: Section 3. Section 164.540 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes is amended to read as follows: (1) The Council on Public Higher Education in Kentucky as defined in KRS 164.010 is hereby designated as the agency of the Commonwealth of Kentucky charged with the responsibility and vested with all necessary…
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, Special Session, 1956, § 3, pp. 63–64
summary: This statute addresses the admission of Negroes to educational institutions in Kentucky. It states that Negroes will not be admitted on an equal basis with other races and that no Negro citizen will be forced to attend a segregated regional institution if an institution offering the same course of study to other races exists within the Commonwealth. It also outlines a program for medical research and education, allowing contracts with medical schools to admit residents of the Commonwealth, with specific provisions for payment and reporting. Several sections of the Kentucky Revised Statutes are repealed.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, ch. 145, pp. 634–646
title: AN ACT relating to education.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, ch. 145, pp. 634–646
summary: This statute amends Section 157.360 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes, which deals with the allocation of classroom units for the foundation program in school districts. It outlines how classroom units are determined based on average daily attendance for elementary, secondary, vocational, and special education, as well as for administrative and support staff. A specific provision is made for Lincoln Institute, stating that one twenty-seventh of a classroom unit shall be included for each pupil in average daily attendance at Lincoln Institute if attendance is under a written contract between the institute and the district of the pupil's legal residence.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, ch. 59, pp. 224–226
title: AN ACT relating to voter registration and purgation.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, ch. 59, pp. 224–226
summary: This act outlines procedures for challenging voter registrations. It specifies that a voter's name can be challenged if they have not voted in two consecutive years. The process involves written notification to the voter, an opportunity to appear before the board to contest the challenge, and the potential for removal from registration lists if the challenge is upheld or if the voter fails to appear. Challenges must be made in writing within ten days after registration books close.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, pp. 86–87
title: AN ACT relating to marriage. Approved February 15, 1960
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1960, pp. 86–87
summary: This act amends Section 402.020 of the Kentucky Revised Statutes to prohibit and void marriages between a white person and a Negro or mulatto. It also outlines other prohibited marriages based on mental capacity, existing marriage, solemnization, and age.

statute_citation: Public Health Laws, 1962, p. 255
title: CHAPTER 402 MARRIAGE
citations: Public Health Laws, 1962, p. 255
summary: This chapter outlines various aspects of marriage law in Kentucky, including prohibited degrees of relationship, void marriages, marriage procedures, license requirements, and age restrictions. Specifically, section 402.020(2) explicitly prohibits marriage between a white person and a Negro or mulatto.

statute_citation: Public Health Laws, 1962, p. 260
title: MARRIAGE § 402.990 Penalties
citations: Public Health Laws, 1962, p. 260
summary: This statute outlines penalties for various marriage-related offenses. Specifically, it states that any party to a marriage prohibited by KRS 402.010 or between a white person and a Negro or mulatto shall be fined and potentially imprisoned if they continue to cohabit. It also details penalties for marrying feeble-minded individuals, idiots, or lunatics, and for unauthorized solemnization of marriages.

statute_citation: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1964, ch. 173, pp. 650–656
title: AN ACT relating to a city/county children's home.
citations: Acts of the General Assembly of the Commonwealth of Kentucky, 1964, ch. 173, pp. 650–656
summary: This act mandates the classification and segregation of inmates in a home for delinquent children based on race, sex, and the nature of their delinquency or conviction. It also emphasizes preventing association between 'good' and 'bad' conduct children.
